chapter: Postwar years, accident and lean times
title: Playing from a chair; the shortened leg and the broken pin
summary: He first played seated on the stand; his left leg is now two inches shorter, requiring a built-up shoe, and the 1950 pin broke a year ago.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Right. Right. When you went back to work at the hotel, Herman, after you'd been in the hospital
Very bad, because they had to take me in a chair. I was sitting in a chair. And they would move me from here in the other room, you know, which was huge.
You couldn't walk.
No. No. And they'd take me, put me up on the stand. Once I was sitting in a chair I could play. Only anybody come up wouldn't know what was happening in this, unless they saw me try to get off.
Now, when I come out (Unintelligible) get me and get me on top of the steps, and my room wasn't too far from there, because it was a hotel room upstairs. And -- and that's the way it went.
I see. With the pin in your leg -- this is -- we're talking about your left leg.
Yes.
Did this leave your left leg shorter than your right leg?
Yes, it's about two inches or more shorter.
What happened to those two inches? Where did they go?
Well, as you can see - see it? see the difference?
Yeah, the knee, the knee comes up
differently.

Yeah, it does that, so I asked my doctor when it happened, was it going to be shorter. He said there was no reason why it should be, because it didn't take out any of the bone. But I found out later from the different people, that usually happens. For some reason the injured leg draws up, and that's why I have to wear a built up shoe, for two inches and something, on that left side. I have my shoes built up. The sole is built up.
Now I'll get up. You see it?
Oh yeah, uh-huh.

So I got to go in there, look, there's a pin there, right in the bridge, in the femur. They got to take it out, and put another one in, or whatever the hell they're going to do, and which I did not want, but I'm in trouble. I'm in pain, most of the time, especially when I'm walking, you know?
So you've gotta do it.
Yeah (inaudible). But this pin, which broke, what, a year ago?
Yeah.
Was -- and that would be 1974, was -- had been in since 1950. So it had been there for 24 years.
Yeah. Uh-huh.
